title: Derived tensor with a scalar-restricted sheaf on a ringed site
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small relative to the universe of module sheaves [def-weil-size-convention], and let $\varphi:\mathcal R\to\mathcal S$ be a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], sheaf tensor and extension of scalars [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], termwise restriction of scalars $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], and derived tensor as obtained by the K-flat localization [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. For every $H\in D(\mathcal R)$ and every sheaf $N$ of $\mathcal S$-modules placed in degree zero, there is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal R)$, natural in both $H$ and $N$,
$$H\otimes_{\mathcal R}^{\mathbf L}\operatorname{Res}_\varphi N\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_\varphi\bigl((H\otimes_{\mathcal R}^{\mathbf L}\mathcal S)\otimes_{\mathcal S}^{\mathbf L}N\bigr).$$
Here the inner extension is valued in $D(\mathcal S)$ as in [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. For any K-flat flat-term representative $P\to H$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], the displayed isomorphism is represented by the balanced chain isomorphism
$$P\otimes_{\mathcal R}\operatorname{Res}_\varphi N\longrightarrow\operatorname{Res}_\varphi((P\otimes_{\mathcal R}\mathcal S)\otimes_{\mathcal S}N),\qquad x\otimes n\longmapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes n,$$
whose inverse sends $(x\otimes s)\otimes n$ to $x\otimes sn$. These representatives compute both derived objects and give the same natural isomorphism independently of the chosen representative. No flatness of $\mathcal S$ over $\mathcal R$, boundedness of $H$, or finite Tor amplitude of $N$ is assumed.

source.place: Step 2, sentence “For such Q, P tensor_A Q = (P tensor_A kappa) tensor_kappa Q”: the ringed-site K-flat balanced tensor identity

proof.text: Restriction of scalars is exact and commutes with small direct sums. Indeed, by [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] it changes only the scalar action, and by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] kernels and cokernels have the same underlying abelian sheaves before and after restriction; the same holds for direct sums. The forgetful functor is faithful, so an underlying zero cohomology sheaf is zero as a module sheaf. Thus termwise restriction preserves quasi-isomorphisms and induces $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi:D(\mathcal S)\to D(\mathcal R)$ by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Tags 03DA (lemma-abelian) and 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits), applied to both coefficient sheaves

proof.text: For an $\mathcal R$-module sheaf $M$ and an $\mathcal S$-module sheaf $N$, construct inverse maps $a_{M,N}:M\otimes_{\mathcal R}\operatorname{Res}_\varphi N\to\operatorname{Res}_\varphi((M\otimes_{\mathcal R}\mathcal S)\otimes_{\mathcal S}N)$ and $b_{M,N}$ by $x\otimes n\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes n$ and $(x\otimes s)\otimes n\mapsto x\otimes sn$. These formulas are first applied to local tensor generators, not to an identification of sheaf-tensor sections with tensor products of sections. Additivity is immediate. The first formula is $\mathcal R$-balanced since $(rx\otimes1)\otimes n=(x\otimes\varphi(r))\otimes n=(x\otimes1)\otimes\varphi(r)n$. The second respects the inner relation $(rx\otimes s)=(x\otimes\varphi(r)s)$ and the outer relation $(x\otimes st)\otimes n=(x\otimes s)\otimes tn$. For $b$, the target $M\otimes_{\mathcal R}\operatorname{Res}_\varphi N$ is a sheaf of $\mathcal S$-modules through $N$: the presheaf tensor $U\mapsto M(U)\otimes_{\mathcal R(U)}N(U)$ is a presheaf of $\mathcal S$-modules, and by [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface] its $\mathcal S$-module sheafification and its $\mathcal R$-module sheafification have the same underlying abelian sheaf; so the second formula is $\mathcal S$-bilinear into an $\mathcal S$-module sheaf, as bilinear extension over $\mathcal S$ requires. The module sheafification universal property [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface] and bilinear extension [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-bilinear-extension], together with the tensor definition [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], therefore give sheaf maps. Their composites are identities on local tensor generators, hence on the sheaves by uniqueness in those universal properties. Both formulas commute with restriction and with module maps; this proves simultaneous naturality.

Apply step 2 with $M=P^i$ in every degree and $N$ in degree zero. Naturality with respect to $d_P^i$ gives a chain isomorphism $a_{P,N}$ with exactly the forward and inverse formulas in the statement. The differential is $d_P\otimes1$ on both sides, since $N$ has only degree zero [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. For a chain map $u:P\to P'$ and an $\mathcal S$-linear map $v:N\to N'$, the two composites in the naturality square both send $x\otimes n$ to $(u(x)\otimes1)\otimes v(n)$. A chain homotopy in $u$ is carried to the corresponding tensor homotopy by the same degreewise formula, so this naturality also holds in the homotopy category.

source.place: Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor), total tensor construction; balanced formula from step 2

proof.text: Choose a representing complex $C$ of $H$ and a quasi-isomorphism $p:P\to C$ with $P$ K-flat and with flat terms using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings], $P_{\mathcal S}=P\otimes_{\mathcal R}\mathcal S$ is K-flat with flat $\mathcal S$-terms, even if $\mathcal S$ is not flat over $\mathcal R$. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], it represents $H\otimes_{\mathcal R}^{\mathbf L}\mathcal S$ in $D(\mathcal S)$, with canonical comparisons natural in maps of resolutions.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat), and 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change), identity topos and coefficient map

proof.text: For a K-flat complex $T$ on either coefficient site, tensoring with $T$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms: if $s$ is a quasi-isomorphism, its cone is acyclic by [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic]; K-flatness [def-pc-kflat-complex] makes its tensor with $T$ acyclic; the cone identification [lem-pc-tensor-mapping-cone-iso] then shows that $1_T\otimes s$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Interchanging the factors uses the symmetry from [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed], with graded sign $(-1)^{ij}$ in total degree $(i,j)$; this sign identifies the two differentials $d_T\otimes1+(-1)^i1\otimes d$ and $d\otimes1+(-1)^j1\otimes d_T$. This gives either tensor order without a flatness assumption on the other complex.

For K-flat flat-term $T$ over a coefficient ring sheaf $B$ and an arbitrary complex $M$, $Q_B\operatorname{Tot}(T\otimes_B M)$ canonically computes $Q_BT\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}Q_BM$. To see this precisely, tensor with $T$ descends in $M$ by step 5 and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. On the K-flat flat-term subcategory its comparison with derived tensor is the canonical natural comparison in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. That subcategory localized at its quasi-isomorphisms is $D(B)$ by the same node; hence the comparison extends uniquely to all $M$ by the localization universal property. For a map $T\to T'$, the naturality square agrees on K-flat flat-term $M$, so uniqueness gives the square for every $M$. In particular, using $T=P$, $M=\operatorname{Res}_\varphi N$, and then $T=P_{\mathcal S}$, $M=N$, proves that the two complexes in step 3 compute respectively the left and right derived objects in the statement, after the exact restriction of step 1. The identification of $Q_{\mathcal S}P_{\mathcal S}$ with the inner scalar extension is step 4.

source.place: Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor) and preceding construction; comparison of one-sided and two-sided K-flat computation

proof.text: Let $\mathcal P_{\mathcal R}$ be the homotopy subcategory of K-flat flat-term complexes. Regard both sides of the desired identity as functors of $H$ with values in the category of functors from $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal S)$ to $D(\mathcal R)$. Steps 3 and 6 give a natural isomorphism between their restrictions along $Q_{\mathcal R}|_{\mathcal P_{\mathcal R}}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], this restriction is a localization at the quasi-isomorphisms. Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], with that functor category as target: the isomorphism and its inverse extend uniquely, their composites extending the identities. The result is therefore natural simultaneously in $H$ and the degree-zero sheaf $N$. For a specified resolution $p:P\to C$, naturality along $Qp$ expresses its component as the chain map $a_{P,N}$ under the canonical computation isomorphisms of steps 4 and 6. Uniqueness shows that any other resolution gives the same component; no direct chain map between the two resolutions is needed. Only the existence of unbounded K-flat resolutions and their preservation under change of rings were used, so no boundedness, finite Tor amplitude, or flatness of the coefficient map is required.

The statement is true and not weakened: unbounded H, arbitrary φ, the coefficient categories D(R)/D(S) and the balanced representative are all kept. I tested it on Z→F_p, Z/4→F_2 (infinitely many Tor groups), φ=id and S=0. Steps 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 follow from what the cited nodes state. Step 5 handles the order of the K-flat factor with the Koszul sign, and I checked that sign. Steps 6 and 7 use only the stated clauses (1)-(3) of the localization lemma and the P_R equivalence from the site-derived-tensor-descent lemma. One fault, fixed: step 2 builds b by S-bilinear extension, but the cited extension lemma needs the target M⊗_R Res N to be an S-module sheaf, and the step did not say why it is one. I added one sentence: the presheaf tensor is a presheaf of S-modules through N, and by lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface its S- and R-sheafifications have the same underlying abelian sheaf. The corrected node is in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-six-functors/; the step is now 1821 characters. There are no new nodes.
